CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sharon Brooks is a 48-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain that occurred four days ago on Sunday while skiing. Patient was attempting moguls when her strap caught on her finger, causing hyperextension and bending of the finger backward. Patient has tried ice and ibuprofen, which has provided minimal relief. Pain is worse with movement.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Constipation. Appendectomy at age 18.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for constipation.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Examination of right index finger reveals tenderness over the distal phalanx and the distal interphalangeal joint. No tenderness over the proximal interphalangeal joint or metacarpophalangeal joint. Patient able to flex and extend finger with pain on flexion. Patient able to touch thumb with index finger.

RESULTS
X-rays of right hand show no fractures. Everything lines up normally.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right hand index finger contusion on the tip of the finger, no fracture. Recommend aluminum foam splint for immobilization. Prescribe Motrin 600 mg every six hours for approximately one week. Patient to call and return if symptoms do not improve.
